## A taste of Mexico

The culinary part of the itinerary takes you to markets, street stalls, family-run restaurants and traditional taquerias. In Coyoacán, food is a way to get to know the neighbourhood, its streets and everyday life. At the San Juan and Medellín markets, you’ll see ingredients at the core of Mexican cooking: different kinds of chillies, maize, mole, spices, herbs, exotic and tropical fruits, fresh vegetables, fish and meat. The stalls also sell flowers, plants, natural remedies and kitchenware. Along the way, there are tastings, fresh juices, hot quesadillas, tacos and mezcal.

The trip goes well beyond food. The canals of Xochimilco recall the days when the Aztecs used waterways to travel across the Basin of Mexico. The pyramids of Teotihuacán, Mexico City’s historic centre, Chichén Itzá, Cobá and Tulum reveal different periods in the country’s history. On the Riviera Maya, ancient cities stand amid the jungle and right beside the Caribbean Sea. After the tours, you can swim in the clear waters of the cenotes.
